decisions.decision: Backfill uses the priority stored when migration runs, so a ticket reprioritized before migration gets the response time for its latest priority.
decisions.alternative: Backfill could use the priority at creation from the ticket's audit history so a later reprioritization has no effect on its original response commitment.

decisions.decision: New tickets get their deadline at creation even while due times are hidden, because the flag gates API exposure and query behavior.
decisions.alternative: Tickets created before activation could receive their first deadline in the migration using the hours selected for rollout.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:7 and 18–20 (R-1 creation rule and R-3 feature gate)

decisions.decision: The work ends with a local source handoff and leaves production backfill, enablement, and verification on production data to the operators.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected delivery to include coordinating and verifying the production rollout with the release manager.

decisions.decision: Operators must stop the service that owns the production file before running the migration against it.
decisions.alternative: Operators could have expected to prepare the backfill from a copy while serving traffic and reconcile changes at cutover.

decisions.decision: An unusable deadline-hours setting makes startup fail with an error naming the variable.
decisions.alternative: The service could warn the operator, use the documented hours for that priority, and start serving requests.

decisions.decision: Backfill leaves the audit history and notification outbox untouched when populating deadlines.
decisions.alternative: The rollout could record the initial deadline assignment in each affected ticket's audit history so agents can see when it was set.

decisions.decision: Deadline data is stored as an optional field on each ticket record in the version-1 JSON file.
decisions.alternative: A deadline map keyed by ticket ID inside the same version-1 file could preserve the exact record shape for tools that consume ticket records directly.
decisions.where: record/02-discovery.md:17 (discovery summary, version-1 optional field); record/03-research.md:12–14 (legacy-reader result and format decision)

decisions.decision: With DUE_TIMES=on, an in-memory store or a new empty store can start without prior migration.
decisions.alternative: The flag could require a prepared persistent file even on an empty instance, so a missing data-file configuration prevents startup.

decisions.decision: The overdue filter runs before cursor pagination, so the page size and next cursor apply to the overdue matches.
decisions.alternative: The filter could screen each ordinary page after pagination, preserving its page boundaries for clients that use them.

decisions.decision: Overdue status is evaluated against the clock for each request, including requests for subsequent cursor pages.
decisions.alternative: A cursor could carry the first page's cutoff time so every page in a scan uses the same definition of overdue.

decisions.decision: The API treats due as a server-assigned field that clients cannot set.
decisions.alternative: Clients could be allowed to echo the exact server-calculated value when submitting ticket objects, while the server still controls the deadline.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9 (R-1, final sentence); repo/docs/api.md:13 (unknown body fields)

decisions.decision: The API returns due as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected the API to return the deadline with the help desk's local offset for display in operator tools.
